key_facts: I have travelled a good deal in Concord
The twelve labors of Hercules were trifling in comparison with those which my neighbors have undertaken
They have no friend Iolas to burn with a hot iron the root of the hydra’s head
pushing before it a barn seventy-five feet by forty
It is said that Deucalion and Pyrrha created men by throwing stones over their heads behind them
Or, as Raleigh rhymes it in his sonorous way
The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
I have lived some thirty years on this planet

forbidden_claims.claim: Thoreau claims in this passage to have lived fifty full years on the planet.
Thoreau compares his neighbors' burdens to the labors of Theseus, aided by his friend Iolas.
Thoreau says his elders handed down treasured guidance he still follows today.

notes: Thoreau says elders gave him nothing useful -- the exact opposite of a claim crediting them with valuable advice. Continues directly after doc 010's cutoff.
